title: How Does Google Maps Know There's Traffic?
sources: Google Keyword blog 'Google Maps 101: How AI helps predict traffic and determine routes' (2020): Maps analyses historical traffic patterns for roads over time and combines them with live traffic conditions from aggregate, anonymized location data of people who have location settings on; works with DeepMind to predict traffic ahead

Wikipedia 'Google Traffic' and Global News 'Does your phone help build Google's traffic maps?': traffic layer is crowdsourced from GPS-determined locations and speeds reported by many mobile phones; Google anonymizes the data
Google Maps Help 'Use layers to find places, traffic...': traffic line colours, green = no traffic delays, orange = medium traffic, red = heavy traffic (darker red = slower)

Hyperallergic, CNN, 9to5Google (Feb 2020): Berlin artist Simon Weckert pulled a red handcart holding 99 second-hand smartphones with Google Maps running slowly through Berlin streets, making Google Maps show a traffic jam (streets turned red) on nearly empty roads

lines.text: How does Google Maps know a road is jammed
lines.caps: HOW DOES *GOOGLE MAPS | KNOW A ROAD | IS *JAMMED

lines.text: There's no camera watching every street.
The secret is phones, like yours.
Phones with location turned on send back how fast they're moving,
lines.caps: PHONES WITH *LOCATION | TURNED *ON | SEND BACK HOW *FAST | THEY'RE *MOVING

lines.text: So when lots of them crawl along one road,
lines.caps: SO WHEN *LOTS | OF THEM *CRAWL | ALONG ONE *ROAD

lines.text: that road turns orange, then red.
Add years of past traffic for that hour,
and it can guess the jam before it happens.
lines.caps: AND IT CAN *GUESS | THE *JAM | BEFORE IT *HAPPENS

lines.text: In twenty twenty, an artist in Berlin
slowly pulled ninety nine phones in a little wagon,
So that traffic jam? It might just be phones.
lines.caps: SO THAT *TRAFFIC JAM? | IT MIGHT *JUST | BE *PHONES
